title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
A man used AI to generate fake obscene images of a college acquaintance by taking her photographs from private social media accounts and morphing them without consent. He then distributed these images across multiple platforms using fake accounts to maintain anonymity. This is a case of AI-enabled image synthesis deployed by an individual outside any organizational context to create nonconsensual intimate imagery.

The abuse was discovered not by system safeguards but by the victim herself, who learned of the harassment through direct messages from anonymous accounts. The attacker had to manually obtain source images, manually upload results to multiple platforms, and manually operate fake accounts across different services. Better access controls on private social media accounts, platform enforcement against coordinated inauthentic behavior using multiple accounts, and detection of known nonconsensual imagery being distributed could have reduced the harm.

It is not established whether the AI tool used had built-in safeguards against this use, whether those safeguards failed, or what other preventive measures the tool's creators had implemented.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and sharing fake obscene images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used artificial intelligence technology to generate inappropriate morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while maintaining anonymity with several Gmail addresses.

The victim discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts informing her that her altered photographs and videos were being circulated on Discord servers. After she reported the case to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi, investigators analyzed digital footprints and traced the fake accounts back to Bansal. During questioning, he admitted that personal resentment from college had motivated him to create and upload the content initially, though other unknown users later created additional explicit images that he reposted. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and other digital evidence as the investigation continues.
